subject: Meteorology
title: Fog Types
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Fog Types.

hook.text: Fog is just a cloud on the ground—but it forms in several distinct ways depending on conditions.

buildup.text: Radiation fog forms on clear, calm nights when the ground cools air to its dew point.

discovery.text: Advection fog forms when warm, moist air moves over a cold surface—like ocean air drifting over cool land.

twist.text: Upslope fog forms when moist air flows up a gentle hill—cooling as it rises until condensation occurs.

climax.text: Steam fog appears when cold air passes over warm water—like the 'steam' rising off a heated pool in winter.

punchline.text: Four ways to make fog—all just clouds at ground level.

quiz.question: How does advection fog form?
options: Warm moist air moving over a cold surface
